claim: On 10 May 1940 the French First Army Group and the British Expeditionary Force advanced into Belgium under Plan D to the line of the Dyle, and the French Seventh Army moved north towards Breda; the German staff expected the Allies to move forward into Belgium.
source: Wikipedia, Battle of France (Plan D, the Dyle line and the Breda variant); the German expectation is the premise of the Manstein Plan.

claim: Halder's diary for 11 August 1941 says that at the outset the staff reckoned with about 200 enemy divisions and had already counted 360; the German estimate before the invasion treated the Red Army as weakened by the purges and poorly equipped.
source: Megargee, Rejecting Catastrophe (NIDS, 2019), citing the Halder diary for 11 August 1941; the pre-war estimate is the standard account and the report's own situation text.

claim: Fremde Heere Ost under Gehlen judged that the main Soviet summer blow of 1944 would fall in the south; Operation Bagration opened on 22 June 1944 against Army Group Centre, which lost most of its strength in the following weeks.
source: Standard accounts of Operation Bagration; the FHO assessment is the report's own premise.

claim: Stalin held that Hitler's main aim was the grain of Ukraine and the coal of the Donbas, and the 1940 plan was redrafted with the weight in the south; in June 1941 Army Group Centre had two of the four panzer groups (the 2nd and 3rd), Army Group North one (the 4th) and Army Group South one (the 1st).
source: Wikipedia, Operation Barbarossa (units involved: 4th in North, 2nd and 3rd in Centre, 1st in South, called Panzer Armies there and Panzer Groups in 1941); the Soviet planning is from the prelude's own claims register (claims/soviet-prelude.json).

claim: Stalin did not believe that Germany would attack in the summer of 1941; the memorandum is dated 15 May and Germany attacked on 22 June 1941, with over three million men.
source: Standard accounts of the warnings of 1941; the date of the memorandum and the strength are those of claims/soviet-prelude.json and the border41 report.

claim: Soviet intelligence identified the attack on the Kursk salient, its axis and approximate date; Operation Citadel opened on 5 July 1943 from both sides of the salient, Army Group Centre from the north and Army Group South from the south.
source: Standard accounts of the Battle of Kursk; the intelligence is the report's own situation text.

claim: The German attack in the west opened on 10 May 1940 and the Meuse was crossed at Sedan on 13 and 14 May; the Allied force at Narvik was evacuated in the first week of June to meet the crisis in France.
source: Wikipedia, Battle of France and Norwegian campaign (the Sedan crossing is from the report's own order of battle on caseYellow40); the evacuation dates are the standard account.

claim: The Prince of Wales and the Repulse were sunk by Japanese aircraft off the coast of Malaya on 10 December 1941, without fighter cover, after Japan attacked Malaya and Pearl Harbor on 7 and 8 December.
source: Standard accounts of Force Z; the report forceZ41 in this game.

claim: The 9th and 10th SS Panzer Divisions of II SS Panzer Corps were refitting near Arnhem in September 1944; Dutch reports and air photographs showed armour there, and the 1st Airborne Division met them.
source: Standard accounts of Operation Market Garden; not reopened against a source in this pass.

claim: Visconti Prasca promised to finish the Greek forces in Epirus and take Preveza in ten to fifteen days; the Italian invasion was stopped inside Greek territory by mid-November 1940, the Greek counteroffensive began on 14 November, and it ended on 6 January 1941 with the capture of the Klisura Pass.
source: Wikipedia, Greco-Italian War.

claim: The Italian camps at Sidi Barrani were not linked into a continuous line; the British attacked on 9 December 1940 through the gap, took Nibeiwa from the rear, and within days the Tenth Army was beaten with tens of thousands of prisoners.
source: Standard accounts of Operation Compass; the gap is the report's own situation text.

claim: On 7 December 1941 the battleships were at their moorings and eight of them were hit; 2,403 Americans were killed; the three carriers were not in the harbor
source: Standard histories; the 2,403 figure is the one the report already gives
note: The consulate's reports as the staff's source is interpretation.

claim: Six of the eight battleships hit were repaired and returned to service; the carriers, shipyards and oil tanks were untouched; American carriers fought at Coral Sea within five months
source: From memory of the standard histories
note: To be checked: the count of six repaired. Yamamoto's estimate is in the report's own text.

claim: Station HYPO read the Japanese plan; Nimitz had Enterprise, Hornet and Yorktown waiting north east of Midway; Yorktown was patched in seventy-two hours
source: Existing Midway battle register (battles-round1.json); NHHC
note: That the staff expected one or two carriers at most is interpretation of the plan's assumption.

claim: Ichiki's first echelon, about 900 men, attacked at the Tenaru river on the night of 20 to 21 August 1942 against prepared Marine positions and most of it was killed
source: Wikipedia, Battle of the Tenaru and Kiyonao Ichiki; HistoryNet
note: Some Japanese scholarship disputes that Ichiki underestimated the American force; the report gives the Army's estimate as the belief, with no number.

claim: Halsey took the Third Fleet's carriers north on 24 October 1944; Ozawa's carriers were sunk off Cape Engano on 25 October; Kurita came through San Bernardino Strait that night
source: Britannica; Naval History and Heritage Command (see battles-round2.json)

claim: The Kikusui attacks sank thirty or more American ships, damaged hundreds and killed nearly five thousand sailors; the fleet stayed until the island was taken in June
source: Wikipedia, Operation Kikusui; NHHC H-Grams on Okinawa (see battles-round2.json)
note: The figures are for the whole campaign, not for the Kikusui attacks alone.

claim: Soryu and Hiryu struck Wake on 21 December 1941 and stood off while the landing went in on 23 December; Pye recalled Task Force 14 on learning of two carriers
source: NPS Marines in WWII, 'Marines at Wake'; Pacific Wrecks chronology; Citizendium
note: Sources differ on the day of the recall (22 or 23 December).

claim: Rochefort's team read AF as Midway and gave the date; the Japanese carriers were found north west of Midway on 4 June and four were sunk
source: Existing Midway battle register (battles-round1.json)
note: That Washington's analysts doubted the reading is the existing node text.

claim: The Marines landed on 7 August 1942 and took the unfinished airfield on the 8th with almost no fighting; the Japanese there were mostly construction troops and had withdrawn
source: HistoryNet; National WWII Museum (see battles-round2.json)
note: The coastwatchers and air photographs as the source is interpretation.

claim: The Mark 14 ran deeper than set and its exploder did not work as designed; the fleet's tests found the faults through 1942 and 1943
source: From memory of the standard histories
note: To be checked against Blair, Silent Victory. The report's own node text gives the Bureau's official position.

claim: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan on 8 August 1945, three months after Germany's surrender, and attacked Manchuria the next day
source: Standard histories; the existing Tehran node text
note: Declaration of war text: jewishvirtuallibrary.org, USSR Declaration of War on Japan.

claim: Rupertus forecast that Peleliu would be taken in a few days (two to four, by different sources); the fighting lasted from 15 September to 27 November 1944
source: Osprey, 'Tragic Peleliu'; Warfare History Network (Haskew); Wikipedia, Battle of Peleliu
note: Sources differ on the forecast: three days, perhaps two; or four days. The report says two to four.

claim: Marine planners asked for ten days of bombardment and were given three; of about 915 fortified positions fewer than 200 had been silenced when the Marines landed
source: Warfare History Network summary of the battle (see battles-round2.json)
note: The 915 and 200 figures are from one account.
